title: What FlashAttention changes
summary: Whether the tiled kernel is exact, and what memory it avoids.

choices.text: It keeps attention inside a fixed local window plus a few global tokens, which is why its memory grows linearly with N while the output stays close to full attention.
It computes standard softmax attention exactly, but it writes the N×N matrix to HBM in smaller chunks, trading extra memory traffic for fewer FLOPs.
It computes standard softmax attention. Q, K, and V are tiled so the N×N matrix is never stored in HBM, and the softmax is accumulated with a running max and sum in on-chip SRAM.
It is exact in the forward pass, but the backward pass still stores the N×N probabilities in HBM, so the memory saving applies only at inference.
